ImageDescription.value: Rang Ghar, located at Rupahi Pathar in Sivasagar, Assam, is known as the first sports pavilion in India. It was originally built in the mid-18th century during the reign of Swargadeo Rudra Singha as a royal sports pavilion for the Ahom kings. Later, between 1744 and 1751 A.D., Swargadeo Pramatta Singha rebuilt the two-storeyed architectural structure.

ImageDescription.value: Construction of Talatal Ghar, the largest monument of the Tai Ahom kingdom, was started in 1707 by the King Rudra Singh once he shifted his capital to Rangpur from Garhgaon. Subsequent kings built upon and enlarged the structure till it reached seven stories – three underground and the balance above it. The British sealed the underground portions and what remains above is just a pale shadow of the old grand palace.

ImageDescription.value: Construction of Talatal Ghar, the largest monument of the Tai Ahom kingdom, was started in 1707 by the King Rudra Singh once he shifted his capital to Rangpur from Garhgaon. Subsequent kings built upon and enlarged the structure till it reached seven stories – three underground and the balance above it. The British sealed the underground portions and what remains above is just a pale shadow of the old grand palace.

Artist.value: Kanad Sanyal

ImageDescription.value:
Maidam - tumuli of the Ahom Kingdom
A unique creation of the Ahom Dynasty of Assam ruling the Ahom Kingdom through 1228 AD to 1826 AD. They buried their kings and members of the royal family in a burrow shaped mound of earth with structures of bricks all around it. The monument resembled the Egyptian pyramids with only the difference of the raw materials used. Hundreds of such maidams are still found scattered all around Assam's Sivasagar district, Dibrugarh, Jorhat and Golaghat districts glorifying the rich cultural traditions of the Ahoms. The Charaideo maidam area is preserved by the ASI as well as by the State Government's agency in two parts as a place of historical importance and it is open for public viewing on weekdays.

ImageDescription.value:
Shiva Dol is a historic 18th-century temple complex in Sivasagar, Assam, comprising Sivadol (dedicated to Lord Shiva), Vishnudol (to Lord Vishnu), and Devidol (to Goddess Durga), along with a museum. Built in 1734 by Queen Bar Raja Ambika during the reign of Ahom king Swargadeo Siva Singha, the temples stand on the banks of the grand Sivasagar Tank (Borpukhuri). The Sivadol, towering at 104 feet and crowned with a golden dome, is the tallest and most prominent, symbolizing the architectural grandeur of the Ahom dynasty.

Shiva Dol is a historic 18th-century temple complex in Sivasagar, Assam, comprising Sivadol (dedicated to Lord Shiva), Vishnudol (to Lord Vishnu), and Devidol (to Goddess Durga), along with a museum. Built in 1734 by Queen Bar Raja Ambika during the reign of Ahom king Swargadeo Siva Singha, the temples stand on the banks of the grand Sivasagar Tank (Borpukhuri). The Sivadol, towering at 104 feet and crowned with a golden dome, is the tallest and most prominent, symbolizing the architectural grandeur of the Ahom dynasty.

ImageDescription.value: স্বৰ্গদেউ শিৱসিংহই প্রথমা ৰাণী বৰৰজা ফুলেশ্বৰী কুঁৱৰীৰ মৃত্যুৰ পাছত তেওঁৰে বিবাহিতা ভনীয়েক দ্রৌপদীক বিবাহ কৰাই অম্বিকা বা মদাম্বিকা নাম দি বৰৰজা পাতিছিল । এইগৰাকী কুঁৱৰীৰ নিৰ্দেশক্ৰমেই সোণৰ ক'লচীৰে সৈতে শিৱদ'ল আৰু শিৱসাগৰ পুখুৰী খন্দোৱা হৈছিল । এই শিৱদ'ল অসমৰ সকলোবোৰ দ'লতকৈ ওখ দ'ল । শিৱদ'লৰ ক'লচীটোত থকা সোণখিনি এৰুৱাই নিবৰ কাৰণে মানে ক'লচীটোলৈ গুলিয়াইছিল, কিন্তু ক'লচীটো বা সোণখিনি খহাব নোৱাৰিলে । ১৯৫০ চনৰ ভূমিকম্পত ক'লচীটো খহি পৰিছিল যদিও ইয়াক আগৰ স্থানত স্থাপন কৰা হৈছিল । শিৱৰাত্ৰিত এই দ'লৰ কাষতে এখন ডাঙৰ মেলা হয়~।

ImageDescription.value: Shiva dol (meaning the temple of the Lord Shiva) is a group of structures comprising three Hindu temples of Sivadol, Vishnudol (meaning temple of the Lord Vishnu) and Devidol (means temple of the Goddess Devi Durga in the local Assamese language) shrines, and a museum. These are located on the banks of the Sivasagar ("the ocean of the god Shiva") tank, also known as the Borpukhuri tank, in the heart of Sivasagar, in the Indian state of Assam.

ImageDescription.value: Sivasagar (previously spelled Sibsagar) (Assamese: শিৱসাগৰ Xiwôxagôr) is a town in the Sibsagar district in the state of Assam in India, about 360 kilometres (224 mi) north east of Guwahati. It is the district headquarters of the Sivasagar district. Sivasagar is a heritage place in Assam famous for the monuments of Ahom kingdom. Now it is a multi-cultural town.

ImageDescription.value: JOYSAGAR TANK,SIVASAGAR, Largest of all the tanks built by Ahom Kings in Assam. It is considered as the largest men made pond in India. The water level of the tanks stays at 14 feet higher than ground level. The Tank Jayasagar was dug by Ahom king Rudrasingha (1696-1714) to commemorate his mother Sati Joymoti, wife of Gadapani, later King Gadadharsingha (1681-1695). The place was chosen, where Siulikpha convicted Joyamoti through his Chaodangs to extract information regarding her exiled husband Gadapani. This is the biggest man-made tank comprising an area of 318 acres including the four banks.

Ghanashyam Dol, a terracotta brick temple near Joysagar Tank, is believed to have been built during King Rajeswar Singha’s reign (1751–1769) for his grandson (naati) of Parbatiya Gosain, earning it the name Naati Gosain Dol. Another account links its origin to King Rudra Singha’s patronage, with Ghanashyam Khanikar credited for its construction.

ImageDescription.value: Fakuwa Doul, built by Swargadeo Rudra Singha (1703–1704) in memory of Queen Joymati Kunwari, stands 30 ft high with a 90 ft circumference. Locals believe it to be her burial mound. With its octagonal plinth, eight Angshikharas, and pyramid-like structure, it remains a unique monument of Assam’s heritage.
